title: Operator Proofflow — Lightweight Playbook (PRD draft)
content:
Purpose:
Provide a compact, actionable PRD draft for a minimal operator-facing proofflow that ties customer-managed-networking changes to immutable audit payloads and approval gates. This doc is intentionally light: usable as a runbook + product sketch for partner pilots.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Minimal evidence envelope to attach to VPC/operator actions
- Approval gate flow for operator-initiated and customer-initiated changes
- Audit log schema recommendations for compact storage and fast query
- On-call runbook for triaging approval/failure cases and evidence collection
- Rollout phases and pilot success criteria

Out of scope (for later PRDs):
- Full forensic archive retention policies across jurisdictions
- UI mockups beyond simple acceptance flows
- Detailed KMS/HSM integration patterns (separate security design doc)

Primary personas:
- Customer network operator (operator): performs firewall/NAT/peering changes inside customer-managed VPCs
- Redwood SRE on-call: triages failed approvals, escalates safe rollbacks
- Customer security reviewer: audits change provenance and evidence bundles

Goals & success metrics:
- Integrate an approval gate that reduces silent misconfigurations by 90% during pilot (measured by post-change incidents)
- Ensure average audit retrieval latency for a single change <= 1s for recent 30-day window
- Compact evidence envelope size <= 8KB per change (for customers with high churn)
- Pilot with 2 customers for 2 months with zero customer-data exposures reported

User stories (example):
1) As an operator, I want to submit a change request that captures the exact CLI/REST command, intent, and an operator signature so auditors can replay and verify.
2) As a security reviewer, I want to query all changes touching subnet X in the last 7 days and filter by approval status.
3) As an SRE on-call, I want automatic rollback triggers when a change causes traffic regression >= 30% in 10 minutes.

High-level approval flow (compact):
- Step 1: Operator creates a change request (CR) via API/CLI. CR includes: change_id, operator_id, change_payload_hash, intent_text, customer_context_id, requested_window.
- Step 2: Automated pre-checks run (schema validation, quick policy engine for obvious failures). If checks pass, CR moves to approval queue.
- Step 3: Approval gate options (configurable per-customer): auto-approve (trusted operator list), manual review (customer reviewer or Redwood policy reviewer), or time-delayed approval.
- Step 4: On approval, the system emits an immutable audit event and a compact evidence envelope is sealed (signed with platform attest key).
- Step 5: Execution agent applies the network change and streams execution events (attempt/start/finish/error) as append-only events linked to change_id.

Compact evidence envelope (design constraints):
- Must be individually verifiable and small.
- Prefer canonical JSON with stable field ordering to keep signatures deterministic.
- Include only essential fields to reconstruct intent: operator_id, timestamp, change_hash, minimal diffs, optional short transcript of pre-check outputs.
- Example envelope text (not literal schema, for illustration):
  {
    "change_id": "CR-20241105-7f9b",
    "operator": "a.chen@redwood.ai",
    "ts": "2024-11-05T16:22:33Z",
    "intent": "scale-gateway-subnet-add-route",
    "payload_hash": "sha256:...",
    "prechecks": ["cidr-ok","peer-exists"],
    "signature": "sig:base64..."
  }

Audit log schema (compact, query-friendly):
- Store rows with fields: [change_id, customer_id, tenant_context, status, approver, ts_submitted, ts_approved, envelope_ref, event_stream_ref]
- Keep a small indexed replica for recent 90 days for fast queries; long-term archive can be compressed blobs.
- For high-frequency customers we recommend delta-minified logs: store full envelope at acceptance, per-event pointers contain only event_type, durable_seq, ts, optional short message (<=256 bytes).

Retention & compression options (pilot knobs):
- default_recent_window: 90 days (hot indexed)
- compact_archive: store gzipped NDJSON of envelopes per day with per-file manifest
- legal-hold: explicit flag to pin envelope files from GC; surfaced to customer UI and compliance API

Telemetry & dashboards (console + ops):
- Per-customer: acceptance_rate, avg_approval_latency, avg_audit_lookup_latency, change_error_rate, rollback_count
- Alerting: SLO breach when avg_approval_latency > 5m for manual flows or > 3x baseline for a given customer
- Tracing: link change_id to request traces and to infra metrics (BGP/peering errors, throughput regressions)

On-call runbook (triage highlights):
- Symptom A: "Change stuck in pending". Steps: check pre-check logs, policy engine rejection reasons, check operator permissions, escalate to customer reviewer contact.
- Symptom B: "Post-change traffic regression". Steps: trigger quick rollback via 'safe-rollback' command, gather envelope and event_stream for last 30s, open incident with customer security and run postmortem template.
- Evidence collection: always attach envelope_ref and the last 50 events from event_stream_ref to incident ticket.

Rollback & safe-fallback semantics:
- All changes must define a rollback candidate (automatic diff inverse) OR be flagged as non-rollbackable.
- Automated safety net: if system-level regressions detected (latency spike, connectivity drop) within acceptance window, execute rollback if enabled.

Pilot rollout (phases):
- Phase 0 (internal): runworkshop with platform/ops team, validate envelope signature lifecycle, run local replay harness.
- Phase 1 (two customers): opt-in pilot with low-churn customers, manual approval flow only, 2-week observation.
- Phase 2 (wider beta): enable auto-approve for trusted operators, add compact-archive, and refine SLO alerts.
- Phase 3 (GA): public API + enterprise contracts and documented retention SLAs.

Acceptance criteria for pilot:
- Evidence envelope produced and verifiable for 100% of accepted changes in pilot tenants.
- Queries for recent changes return within 1s 95th percentile.
- On-call runbook validated by at least one simulated regression exercise per customer.

Open questions / risks:
- How should signatures be rotated and notarized for customer-managed change agents? (security input required)
- Jurisdiction-specific retention rules — must be surfaced in customer onboarding (legal to weigh in).
- Edge-case: customer applies same change outside Redwood control (drift) — how to reconcile duplicate events? Suggest a drift-detection utility.

Next steps (immediate):
- Schedule 90-min design review with Security and SRE (owner: Liam Chen) — target week of 2024-11-18.
- Prototype envelope signer and simple query index in infra sandbox (owner: Mateo).
- Draft customer pilot onboarding checklist and contact template for two pilot customers (owner: Aisha).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally concise and operational. Think of this doc as a shared runbook + lightweight PRD — it should be easy to hand to a partner engineering lead to run with minimal further specs.
- Please comment on required fields in the envelope and whether a binary-minimized envelope (CBOR) is preferable for some customers.

References & contextual links:
- Confluence sketch (linked above) contains longer approvals taxonomy.
- Related JIRA: JIRA-PD-4123 (approval-gates core), JIRA-PD-4211 (compact-archive prototype).
